ev.q: As of April 2024, 83% of persons with chronic hepatitis C have received a diagnosis
By April 2024, among 130,000 persons estimated to have current chronic HCV infection in Georgia, 107,604 (82.8%) had received a diagnosis
from 132 to 52 per 100,000 persons among the general non-PWID population
The 2021 nationwide serologic survey found HBsAg seroprevalence of 0.03%
indicating a 67% decrease in prevalence compared with 5.4% in 2015
This report describes the progress made during April 2015–April 2024 toward achieving hepatitis B and hepatitis C elimination in Georgia.
leading to a 61% decrease in the estimated annual incidence of new chronic HCV infections
